4b. Midland swap classes vs their Delaware analogue (D134 B: card only a class clearly unlike it)

Same detector, same sql/23 audit, same code, both basins pulled the same day (Midland as-of 2026-09-01, Delaware as-of 2026-08-01). Test stated before any card was drawn: a class with ≥ 20 Midland flags and ≥ 10 Delaware flags is unlike when its flag rate is ≥ 2× or ≤ 1/2× the Delaware's, or sql/23 concurrence or the GOR own-vote share differs by ≥ 25% points, or the median own-band TVD offset is ≥ 1.5× or ≤ 1/1.5×. no analogue = fewer than the minimum Delaware flags: the rule's default (uncalibrated → tag kept) applies, as it would in the Delaware. small = too few Midland flags to judge.

4c. Allocation-well screen (plan Phase 3 difference 6)

Twin laterals touching the family (≥ 80% of the shorter stick within 150 ft of the other, |ΔTVD| ≤ 150 ft): stacked pair 22, twin 13, re-drill 10. stacked pair = two benches down one surface path; re-drill = one side never reached 12 months or first production > 180 d apart; twin = same bench, both producing, first production within 180 d. Split signature (El Campeon) = a twin whose low side holds < 50% of the high side's 12-mo oil at the same GOR (within ×1.2): 0 in the family. Detector check: on the Delaware pull it puts 22 of the 46 recorded El Campeon / Los Vaqueros exclusions in a coinciding same-bench pair (14 as twins, 10 with the split signature; the rest pair with a twin whose TVD or first production differs beyond the thresholds, or one side never reached 12 months) — the screen is a review list, not a filter.
